# Foundations of Inference {#sec-theory-inference}

Part I asked you to operate an inference service. This chapter asks why it
behaves as it does. We move from dashboards to the models underneath:
what a forward pass computes, why batching and caching pay off, and what
limits decoding speed in principle.

By the end you will be able to explain the latency and throughput behavior
you measured in @sec-eng-inference from first principles.

## The forward pass

Inference as a sequence of tensor operations, the arithmetic intensity of
each, and where the time provably goes.

## Autoregressive decoding

The probabilistic model behind next-token prediction, why generation is
sequential, and the exact redundancy the key-value cache removes.

## Roofline and the throughput limit

Compute bound versus memory bound, the roofline model, and why batching
moves a workload along it.

$$
\text{intensity} = \frac{\text{FLOPs}}{\text{bytes moved}}
$$

## Sampling and decoding

Temperature, top-$k$, top-$p$, and what each does to the output
distribution, with the bias and variance each introduces.

## Speculative and parallel decoding

Trading extra compute for fewer sequential steps, and the conditions under
which speculative decoding is provably faster.

## Approximation and error

What quantization and low-rank approximation do to the function the model
computes, and how to bound the resulting error.
